sentences.english: The small dog searches for food.
The dog makes for the town.
In the town, the dog sees food.
At the table, the farmer has food.
The dog sees the farmer.
For the dog seeks the food.
The farmer sees the faithful dog.
And so the farmer gives the food to the dog.
The dog carries the food to the forest.
The dog loves the faithful farmer.

sentences.latin: Fēmina parva sed fortis marītum habet.
sentences.english: The small yet strong woman has a husband.

sentences.latin: Marītus scūtum magnum ad portam portat.
sentences.english: The husband carries the large shield to the gate.

sentences.latin: Itaque fēmina marītō gladium longum dat.
sentences.english: And so the woman gives the husband a long sword.
The husband has the long sword.

sentences.latin: In viā populus lapidem magnum videt.
sentences.english: In the road, the people see a large stone.
The husband takes the stone.

sentences.latin: Fēmina lapidem ā suō marītō capit.
sentences.english: The woman takes the stone from her own husband.
The woman lifts and carries the stone.

sentences.latin: Populus fēminam fortem videt et laudat.
sentences.english: The people see and praise the strong woman.
The husband's friend sees the strong woman.
But the friend envies the woman's courage.

sentences.latin: In agrō amīcus fēminam ad arborem magnam dūcit.
sentences.english: In the field, the friend leads the woman to a large tree.
The woman lifts the large tree.
And so the friend gives the woman a gift.
The friend believes the woman.
The husband praises his own wife.
The woman opens the heavy gate of the town.
The gate is opened by the woman.

sentences.latin: Fēmina et marītus ā populō laudantur.
sentences.english: The woman and the husband are praised by the people.

sentences.latin: Itaque marītus fēminam suam fortem amat.
sentences.english: And so the husband loves his own strong wife.

sentences.latin: In scholā magister sapiēns frātrem et sorōrem docet.
sentences.english: In the school, the wise teacher teaches the brother and the sister.

sentences.latin: In librō magnō frāter verba difficilia magistrī sapientis scrībit.
sentences.english: In the big book, the brother writes the wise teacher's difficult words.

sentences.latin: Magister sapiēns sorōrem fortem dē verbīs difficilibus librī monet.
sentences.english: The wise teacher warns the strong sister about the book's difficult words.

sentences.latin: Soror sapiēns omnia verba difficilia librī magistrō dīcit.
sentences.english: The wise sister tells the teacher all the difficult words of the book.

sentences.latin: Itaque frāter fortis et soror sapiēns ā magistrō sapientī laudantur.
sentences.english: And so the brave brother and the wise sister are praised by the wise teacher.
